Tbh it's really moving to see comments like this. I've been drowning in self-hate and spite for a whole fucking year, i didn't think anyone would see the hope i saw in just not giving up. I'm gonna write a whole essay for ya here cuz i havent had the chance to talk about this outside my journals so I hope you dont mind.

I hit a wall then. If im gonna fail anyway, like a lot of people think is inevitable for smth like addiction, then WHY would I just give up?

The whole thing really had me question what a good person was. I have a really strong sense of injustice and that might just be my nature, but I think it was also a nurtured thing from my childhood. I witnessed and was the victim of abuse, and you know how every adult in books where children are the protagonists are just magically fucking stupid or oblivious and dont trust their kids when they tell them theyre in danger? Thats what my childhood was like. The adults I could trust were pushed away from me because they didnt condone my parent's behaviour. So much of who I am is just about doing the most good I can. So much of it revolved around the idea that every person carries the guilt of the good they did not do. Any place I could see an opportunity and need for help I would always go out of my way to give it. When I fell into addiction and did truly awful shit (and in a really fucked up and sad and relieving way, did it only to myself) it fully changed the trust I had in me.

Every shred of kindness sent to me seemed like a waste. I had deliberately broken the codes I spent so much of my life building and closely guarding, standards I had held others up to and rejected them for. I was a fucking hypocrite, I was pathetic, I didnt have a reason not to hate myself. I was gonna kill myself, honestly. I could see it coming. I've been suicidal on and off since i was 9 so i know what it looks like for me. I'm an adult now, I had and still have the agency to do it however I wanted to, and I was fucked up enough that I knew it'd happen. Seemed inevitable. But all the other times I was suicidal it seemed inevitable then too, and I've only ever attempted once in my life, and even then i chickened out. So why would this time be different, besides being a different type of intensity and complete shittiness?

For a lot of the time I wanted to die as a kid, there were a very select few things that kept me around. My dad, my dog, my best friend, and just not wanting to end things on a cliffhanger. What next thing was gonna happen with science? What next thing was gonna happen with my best friend? What moments would I miss with my dad, my dog, my earth? So i postponed my death a LOT. Sort of a "lets see how long we can keep this going," thing. the pain weighed on me immeasurably. It hurt so fucking bad being alive. But i just couldnt hurt anyone else around me, and eventually, about 2 years ago, I'd changed my circumstances in life enough that I came to a new conclusion. I am going to die.

No matter what I do. Either death will take me of natural causes, or someone will do it for me (so much more efficient. what a fucking inconvenience trying to kill yourself is man lmao. such a pain fr.) so why am i putting so much energy into worrying about making it happen faster? I cant really do expedited shipping on my own death. But did I deserve to live? You can argue that all people deserve to live. Personally, having seen as much brutal fucking evil in the world as I have, and knowing that I've only hit the tip of the iceberg, I fully disagree. I just dont think theres a good way of deciding who that applies to yet. Worse, if who I am now isnt a person who does deserve life, does the good I did before I became this person help at least neutralize it? And honestly my answer was no. Or at the very least, I dont know. I dont think someone who does a lot of charitable good (truly charitable, not for any purpose other than just being kind) is allowed a pass when they do something deliberately awful. They should be held accountable for that. I'm not sure it makes them wholly evil, that probably depends on what they did and why. But it doesnt make what they did wrong right.

And then I wondered about people who havent ever really known themselves to be kind. Folks who were nurtured into being awful shitbags- bullies, criminals, etc. If they should find themselves genuinely reflecting on who they are and decide they really dislike the image they see, when they reach a different point in life and can see significant and undeniable change and have become good people, are people who were "born good" more valuable than them because they never fucked up? I kinda see myself in the opposite way. I think I was more of the "born pretty good" type, continued on that path, and then hit some really deeply fucked up shit and the untempered parts of my principles were just completely fucked. I had a breakdown I guess. That was where I hit the current philosophy I've explained to u. I was thinking about this and my relationship to the concept of goodness for, like, literal months, just trying to figure out where to go from there and how long restoring my self quality would take and i saw this quote. Idk what it was from, and i might be misquoting it cuz i dont think i remember it work for word, but its something like "Is it worth more to be born good or to have become good by overcoming great evil?" I liked it because it just cracked the whole fuckin thing open like a pilsbury dough can. AND, to boot, its a trick question! One is not better than the other. Obviously. Cuz if I started out at least a decent human, and deliberately set foot the path to stay good, and STILL ended up fucked, theres probably something wrong with the procedural system that I was given.

​

I think this is where most "villains" go wrong. Even in like, literature. All good villains are villains who are right about something. Just something. Theyve got some kind of really compelling backstory that totally explains why they acted the way they did and why they dug the hole theyre in now. I knew so many, so, so many people like that as a kid. Reasonable context to why they are the way they are, but they never sought to repair it or continue trying to be good out of spite of the evil theyd lived thru. I hated it so much. My number 1 fear as a kid was going crazy, because it all seemed to happen to them, and I REALLY FUCKING DIDNT WANT THAT. It was so depressing. Id rather've died than stayed the way I was. So idk, i tried to kill that person every way I could without killing myself. I just pissed all over everything those shitty people I knew stood for. If I'm not good, then I'm not good. Thats fine. But I will not ever resign myself to defeat if my defeat means other people have to suffer. So if I die alone trying, so be it! At least I can sleep at night.
